decision: Build an expected-value bot with an opponent model
why: Exploit the many simple bots expected in a student field while staying sensible
evidence: Beat every fixed-style test bot in nearly every match

decision: Train a CFR solver on an abstraction of the game
why: A balanced strategy is the strongest thing a rival team could build; we needed one to test against and to learn from
evidence: solver/NOTES.md: 758,044 information sets, discounted CFR on 19.2 M deals
result: cfrS, used as a test opponent and inside the entry

decision: Measure the EV bot against the solver
why: Find the main threat
evidence: EV bot lost about 1.2 chips per hand to the solver over whole 1,000-hand matches

decision: Hybrid: solver plays the first share of each match, EV bot the rest
why: Let the EV bot learn before it takes over
evidence: 1,000-hand matches vs the solver: 11/40 and 14/40 against 15/40 and 12/40 for the EV bot alone

decision: Solver check: drop an option kind the solver plays under a threshold
why: Keep the EV bot's exploitation close to sound play
evidence: 345 of 380 test matches won against 326 for the EV bot alone; thresholds 2%, 5%, 10% tried

decision: Solver check from preflop too
why: Preflop mistakes against solvers were the largest remaining loss
evidence: +20 points (se 7.7) over 308 Stage 2 matches

decision: More flop runouts (480 instead of 240)
why: Less noise in flop equities
evidence: +12 points (se 7.6) alone; on top of step 6: -2 (se 6.6)
result: Rejected (no gain once step 6 is in)

decision: Remove the lead lock
why: Two-leg rules: a leg cannot see the other leg's chips, so a lead is never safe to fold out
evidence: Same moves as before on fixed seeds (identical match logs)

decision: Softmax temperature halved or doubled
why: Test sensitivity
evidence: +5 (se 5.6) and +6 (se 4.9): both directions 'better', a sign of shared-deal luck

decision: Review fix: a small re-raise late in a round was read as an all-in by the solver tree
why: The solver check then removed every option but fold or call
evidence: vs small re-raisers: +3 points (se 2.6), +172 capped chips per match (se 86); general field -4 (se 9.4) over 488 matches

decision: Review fix: discard named by card identity
why: Protects against a reordered hole-card list
evidence: No change with the current engine

decision: Review fix: the big blind's preflop check ends the street
why: Its value had included a bet that cannot come
evidence: Part of step 10's tests

decision: 14-bot Stage 2 round robin
why: Check the entry against the strongest opponents together
evidence: 91.0 of 104 points; next best 69.0 (results/round_robin_stage2.txt)

decision: Bots written to beat the entry with its code in hand
why: Find weaknesses a real opponent could hit by accident
evidence: Small-bet attacker: entry won 28/32 long matches. Trap attacker: 16/32 long, 15/32 short

decision: Solver check off after the flop against fixed-rule discarders
why: The solver assumes the opponent threw away its worst card
evidence: vs such bots: -12 points (se 3.3) Stage 2, -12 (se 4.6) Stage 1, 96 matches each

decision: Preflop table with exact card removal
why: The table counted opponent hands sharing a card with ours (+1.6 to +1.9 points of equity for K-K-Q)
evidence: lab/gen_pre2.py with a brute-force self-test
result: Rejected: +256 chips per long match against f7 (se 123), but no gain on the general field (+3 points, se 7.3) and -6 (se 6.9) on top of cand36

decision: Slow-play rate learnt as P(passive | strong hand)
why: It was learnt as P(strong hand | passive), too small by about P(strong) / P(passive)
evidence: Same prior, so play before the first showdown is unchanged
result: Rejected: -4 points (se 4.2) long and -3 (se 5.4) short against the trap bot it targets

decision: Three corrections where real bets meet the solver tree
why: Min bets mapped onto a third-pot bet forced folds; all-in-only nodes dropped every raise size; a 4% cut split raise shares
evidence: lab/candidates/fix24.py

decision: No solver check when there is nothing to call
why: Against callers the check blocked value bets and forced bluffs
evidence: Step 15 showed removing the check can lose chips; needs the strongest evidence
result: Not adopted: not tested further, and step 15 showed removing the check can lose chips

decision: Treat a bet that leaves under a fifth of the pot behind as an all-in, and stop counting folds to a re-raise that costs the opponent almost nothing
why: A copy of the bot that bets all-in minus 2 chips beat cand20 in 31 of 32 long matches: the solver check was off for such bets and a 2-chip all-in re-raise was given 30% fold equity
evidence: results/near_allin_attacker.txt: +16 points of 32 (se 3.2) long, +11 (se 3.7) short; general field +5 (se 7.3)

decision: Read the range after a rare aggressive action from the measured share of weak hands
why: The share of weak hands seen behind shown bets was used as a per-hand weight, so a bet made 10% of the time was read as 57% weak where 15% were; re-raises over turn big bets lost 48 chips each (se 13)
evidence: results/big_bet_attackers.txt: +32 points over 128 deal sets (se 7.5) against value big-bet bots; 0 (se 5.1) against big-bet bluffers; results/cand36_vs_cand29_field.txt +11 (se 7.0) long, -3 (se 9.1) short

decision: A call at the raise cap or with us all-in is not read as passive; the call EV takes the call off the stack once
why: Both found by replaying logged decisions against the engine's state
evidence: Too small to measure alone; inside cand36's tests

decision: Re-raise over a bet above 1.2x the pot only with a strong hand
why: Alternative to step 21
evidence: +20 points (se 8.1) against value big-bet bots, less than step 21, and logs against strong bots show these re-raises win there

decision: Separate counters for acting first and acting after our check or limp
why: One counter held both decisions (P(big blind raises our limp) read 0.58, true 0.36)
evidence: -2.5 points (se 4.6) against bots that raise every limp

decision: No solver check for bets far cheaper than the tree size they map to
why: A min-raise was read as the tree's pot-size open
evidence: -88 capped chips per long match (se 65) against min-raise bots

decision: Read range slices inside equity buckets; round solver features as the trainer did
why: Both correct by brute-force checks
evidence: results/cand41_vs_cand36_field.txt: short matches +20 points (se 8.5) and +56 capped chips per match (se 20), 9 of 10 strong bots better; long matches -4 (se 6.9); blind rivals -1 (se 3.3)

decision: Test against rivals written blind from the official documents
why: Every earlier rival had been seen while tuning
evidence: results/blind_rivals.txt: cand36 won 29 and 28 of 32 long matches, 27 and 18 of 32 short ones

decision: On the flop, slice the opponent range in the same order its actions are read (3-card strength)
why: The equity view sorted kept pairs by pair strength while the action model slices 3-card hands (top-15% equity gap up to 0.24 while the discard model is unsure)
evidence: -2 points (se 6.6) long, -3 (se 9.0) short over 240 matches each

decision: Retrain the solver with a non-all-in 4-bet preflop and a non-all-in 3-bet after the flop
why: The old tree had only all-in at those raise levels, so smaller re-raises were mapped onto all-in
evidence: -1 point (se 7.3) long, -5 (se 8.3) short over 240 matches each; against min-raise bots -1 (se 1.7) over 48

decision: No solver check facing an all-in
why: Facing an all-in the solver check vetoed calls that the bot's own read of this opponent's shoving range rated worth making
evidence: results/candidates_after_cand41.txt: +5 points (se 8.3) and +53.8 capped chips per match (se 62.5) over 176 long matches against near-all-in and overbet attackers

decision: Count each preflop action once in the opponent model
why: Preflop the pooled counter and the street counter held the same counts, so each preflop action was counted twice
evidence: results/candidates_after_cand41.txt: 0 points (se 1.4) over 64 long matches against preflop-aggression bots, -2 (se 2.0) over 64 against style-switching bots

decision: Separate counters for the limper facing our raise
why: One counter held two answers: the limper's to our raise and the big blind's to our open; cand20 folded far more often as a limper
evidence: results/candidates_after_cand41.txt: -8 points (se 5.2) over 64 long matches against cand20

decision: Separate counters for the answer to our first bet after the opponent checked
why: One counter held the answer after the opponent checked and the answer when we bet first; after a check, test bots folded more and raised less
evidence: results/candidates_after_cand41.txt: blind rivals +1 point (se 3.6) over 64 long and -4 (se 4.7) over 64 short matches, with fewer wins against f17 (26 vs 27 long, 18 vs 22 short); general field -2 (se 6.3) over 240 long; together with step 32: 0 against cand20 (se 4.7), +4 general field (se 7.1), 0 and 0 against the blind rivals (se 3.5 and 4.9)
result: Not shipped: no gain against the bots it targets

decision: Skip the discard result when a time panic left no flop tables
why: Under 1000 ms of bank the bot discards before building the flop tables; the next message raised a caught TypeError and wrote a stderr line every hand
evidence: results/time_panic_cand49.txt: with the bank cut to 900 ms, 181 stderr lines before and 0 after; release checks (engine_checks_cand49.txt, numpy_versions_cand49.txt, slow_core_cand49.txt): 17 matches, 0 forfeits, 0 notices, 0 stderr lines

decision: Skip a message line that is valid JSON but not an object
why: main() read msg.get("type") outside its try block, so a line such as [] or null would have ended the process, a forfeit; the organisers' engine sends only objects
evidence: results/input_guard.txt: cand49 exits with code 1, cand50 with 0; match logs identical to cand49 on three fixed deal sets (lab/eqcheck.sh)

decision: Count the opponent's first action on a street after the flop by position
why: One counter held two decisions, opening the street out of position and answering our check; a practice bot that always checks first and always bets when checked to won 27 of 32 long and 23 of 32 short matches against cand49
evidence: results/practice_bots_night.txt: +14.0 match points (se 3.2) over 32 long and +11.0 (se 3.7) over 32 short matches against that bot; results/cand55_vs_cand41_field.txt: general field +4.0 (se 6.5) long, -3.0 (se 8.6) short; blind rivals +3.0 (se 3.6) long, +2.0 (se 4.7) short
result: Kept (build/fix43.py; tested as cand53, same moves)

decision: Separate counters for 0.66-pot and pot-sized bets
why: Opponents fold 13 to 28 points more often to a pot-sized bet than to a 0.66-pot one, but the two sizes shared one counter, so bluffs took the smaller size and value bets the larger
evidence: results/size_slots.txt: on top of the position counters, +2.0 points (se 2.5) against the blind rivals over 64 long matches and -3.0 (se 1.7) long, +5.0 (se 3.6) short against the new rivals; below the 2-se bar set before the results

decision: No change for bet-size and discard tells
why: Our 0.66-pot bets were mostly weak and our pot-sized bets mostly strong; a practice bot built with our code in hand read our hand from them and from our discard
evidence: results/practice_bots_night.txt: level with cand49 over 64 matches (cand49 won 14 of 32 long and 18 of 32 short)

decision: Recount every number in README and results from the raw rows
why: A check made without first reading the published values
evidence: 842 claims: 833 reproduced; 9 corrected (stale Stage 1 blind-rival lines, peak memory 77 MB, river decisions 16,000, one se, two chip figures, the review count)

decision: Keep cand55; do not add the flop fold rule of f21
why: f21 (cand53 plus: on the flop, out of position, after checking, fold to a bet unless equity is at least 0.45) placed first in the 12-bot round robin, 37 of 44 points to 33; rule set before the follow-up: adopt only if f21 beats cand55 head to head, or cand53 on the general field, by more than 2 se
evidence: results/f21_followup.txt: cand55 won 37 of 64 long and 19 of 32 short matches against f21; f21 minus cand53 on the general field +2.0 points (se 6.5); results/round_robin_12.txt

decision: Review round of cand55: six independent reviews (two rules and forfeit audits, the decision logic, a fuzzer with odd opponents, two searches for habits an opponent could read); every finding tested on the server before any change
why: The entry is frozen only after a full review round finds nothing that survives a server test
evidence: results/review_round_8nov.txt
result: Two fixes (steps 42 and 43), one habit left (step 44)

decision: One BLAS thread, and three crash paths closed (build/fix44.py)
why: When NumPy loads, its BLAS library starts one thread per visible core and each reserves address space: 672 MB on 14 cores, and cand55 did not start under a 512 MB address-space cap. A byte that is not UTF-8, JSON nested too deep to parse, or a request without legal actions or hole cards ended the process
evidence: results/review_round_8nov.txt: cand72 runs 1 thread, reserves 140 MB and starts under a 256 MB cap

decision: No solver check when the real price to call is under 0.8 of the price the solver's tree answered (build/fix45.py)
why: A copy of cand55 that bets the minimum where it would check beat it by 316 chips per long match (se 96): the tree has no bet that small, so the solver's advice answered a dearer bet and forced folds. Rule set before the results: remove most of the copy's gain, and no stage worse than -2 se on the general field, the blind rivals and fresh deals
evidence: results/cand72_vs_cand55_field.txt: against the copy +1,128 chips per match (se 115), 53 of 60 won; general field +1.0 points (se 6.4) long and -8.0 (se 8.8) short; blind rivals -2.0 (se 3.5) and +5.0 (se 4.3); fresh 14-bot field -14.0 (se 12.2) over 840 long and -4.5 (se 15.8) over 840 short matches

decision: All-in habit not fixed in cand72
why: A bot that calls an all-in only with its strongest hands gained 96 capped chips per long match over a control bot that reads nothing (se 37); every logged preflop open-shove came from the top 3 to 4% of hands
evidence: results/review_round_8nov.txt: cand55 still won 57 of 60 against it
result: Open: a candidate without the preflop shove is under test

decision: Entry is cand72
why: Every gate set before the results passed, and the release checks are clean: 11 matches on the organisers' engine with 0 notices and 0 stderr lines, NumPy 1.26 and 1.23 clean, slowed CPU 25.7 s of 30 and 64.7 s of 75 per leg, no move that loses whatever the opponent holds in 4,014 river decisions
evidence: results/engine_checks_cand72.txt, slow_core_cand72.txt, numpy_versions_cand72.txt, audit_cand72.txt; zip md5 a5a85420, bot.py md5 90d54a19
